citation.title: Accelerating metamaterial topology optimization using deep super-resolution networks
citation.authors: Ajendra Singh, Shubham Saurabh, Abhinav Gupta, Rajib Chowdhury

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: After training, low-resolution optimization plus super-resolution takes about 5–7% of the compute time of a same-resolution high-resolution SIMP run for the studied metamaterials.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Abstract gives 5–7% of conventional cost (a range of roughly 14.3–20×); §4.1 Table 1's first detailed comparison gives 457 s / 24 s = 19.0417× for bulk modulus.
claim.alternatives: §4 Tables 3, 5, 7 report analogous time savings for shear modulus, elastic modulus and Poisson's ratio.

baseline.classical_method: SIMP topology optimization with optimality criteria and energy-based homogenization
baseline.implementation: §4: FEniCS 55-line Python topology optimization code cited as [82]
baseline.hardware_classical: §4: Intel Xeon 6230 and NVIDIA Quadro P2200 system; allocation by method not stated
baseline.hardware_ml: §4: Intel Xeon 6230 and NVIDIA Quadro P2200 system; allocation by method not stated
baseline.problem_size: abstract, §4.1: 48×48 low-resolution and 192×192 high-resolution 2D unit-cell meshes
baseline.classical_iterations: §3.1 Algorithm 1: stops on criterion, numerical threshold not stated
baseline.classical_time: §4 Tables 1, 3, 5, 7: bulk 457 s, shear 493 s, elastic 438 s, Poisson 386 s (averages)
baseline.ml_time: §4 Tables 1, 3, 5, 7: low-resolution optimization plus prediction takes bulk 24 s, shear 26 s, elastic 28 s, Poisson 24 s (averages)
baseline.data_generation_cost: §3.1: 1,000 paired low/high-resolution SIMP designs per objective (4,000 total); time not stated
baseline.quality_metric: §3.4: homogenized objective recomputed after meshing returned design, plus volume-fraction error, MSE and IoU
baseline.quality_gap: §4.1 Table 2: bulk objective error 3.03% and volume-fraction error 1.95%; §4.2 Table 4: shear objective error 1.57% and volume error 1.04%; §4.3 Table 6: elastic objective error 2.34% and volume error 1.91%; §4.4 Table 8: Poisson objective error 4.24% and volume error 1.57% (averages).

R1.evidence: Abstract and §4 Tables 1–8: shorter ML-route times are compared with fully optimized high-resolution SIMP although average objective and volume errors remain nonzero; no matched quality or time budget is reported.

R2.evidence: §4 identifies one Xeon/GPU machine and a 55-line FEniCS classical implementation, but gives no solver or CPU/GPU allocation by method, or hardware-matching rationale; no R2(a–e) criterion is established.

R3.evidence: §3.1 says training uses 4,000 optimization-derived paired designs and calls preparation/training a one-time cost; §4's time tables exclude both costs and provide no duration or break-even use count.

R4.evidence: §3.4 says returned predicted images are remeshed and physically re-analyzed for homogenized objective; §4 reports volume errors, but no failed or infeasible design rate.

reporting.n_test_cases: §3.1, §4: 150 held-out samples per objective, four objectives (600 test samples total)

notes: The cited 55-line FEniCS data generator is prior published code, not public code for the proposed EDSR method. Times include generating the low-resolution input but exclude offline paired high-resolution optimization and model training.
